dialogue_stages.tutor_prompt: When two pairs of parallel lines intersect, how do the intersection angles at different vertices relate to each other?
dialogue_stages.student_response: They must all be either equal to the given angle or supplementary to it, because translations keep lines parallel.
dialogue_stages.tutor_feedback: Correct! Dual parallelism partitions all 16 planar angles across the four vertices into exactly two equivalence classes: acute angles of measure x and obtuse angles of measure 180° - x.

dialogue_stages.tutor_prompt: If an angle between intersecting parallel lines is x, and the adjacent angle on a straight line is bisected into two equal angles y, write the formula expressing y in terms of x.
dialogue_stages.student_response: The adjacent angle on the straight line is 180° - x. Since it is split into two equal angles y, we have y + y = 180° - x, so 2y = 180° - x, which gives y = (180° - x)/2 = 90° - x/2.
dialogue_stages.tutor_feedback: Spot on derivation! You correctly identified the linear pair supplement and divided the remainder by 2.

dialogue_stages.tutor_prompt: What happens as x approaches 90° (lines become perpendicular)? Does your formula hold?
dialogue_stages.student_response: If x = 90°, then y = 90° - 90°/2 = 90° - 45° = 45°. Since the supplementary angle is 180° - 90° = 90°, bisecting 90° gives exactly 45°. The formula holds perfectly at the perpendicular boundary.
dialogue_stages.tutor_feedback: Brilliant verification. Boundary testing at x = 90° confirms algebraic and geometric consistency.
